options.content: Sending information over a distance by electronic means
Carrying letters and parcels by road and rail

stem: Which type of service provider supplies landline telephones through cables to offices?

A courier company
An insurance company
A commercial bank

stem: Which is the main advantage of email over an ordinary telephone call for confirming an order?

stem: A wholesaler wants to hold a meeting with branch managers in Bulawayo, Mutare and Masvingo without anyone travelling. Which service is most suitable?

A fax message to each branch
A notice on the head office board

explanation: Video conferencing allows a live, two-way meeting and saves travel time and cost.

options.rationale: Sending documents is what fax does.

stem: A tuck-shop owner sells US\$1,250 of airtime in a month and earns 4% commission. Calculate her commission for the month.

A trader used to make 6 return trips a month to Harare to place orders, at US\$14 a trip. She now places all her orders by phone, spending US\$9 a month on airtime and data. Calculate her monthly saving.
explanation: Old cost = 6 × US\$14 = US\$84. Saving = US\$84 − US\$9 = US\$75.
hints: Find the old cost of travelling, then subtract the new cost of phoning.

stem: Explain **two** ways in which mobile phones have helped small traders in Zimbabwe.

points.description: Way 1, e.g. ordering stock / contacting suppliers without travelling.
Explained: saves time and transport costs; shelves restocked quickly.
Way 2, e.g. receiving payments by mobile money / advertising on messaging groups / selling airtime.
Explained: fewer lost sales when customers lack cash / reaches more customers / extra income.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Traders can order stock from suppliers by phone or message, so they no longer travel to town, saving fares and time away from the stall. They can also accept mobile money, so they do not lose sales when customers have no cash.

explanation: Mobile phones help with ordering, payment, advertising and extra income.
hints: Think about buying stock, selling and getting paid.

stem: Nyasha runs a busy hardware shop in Kwekwe. At present the shop has one landline telephone. Customers complain that the line is often engaged, and Nyasha writes orders from contractors on paper while she talks. She is considering getting an internet connection, an email address and a business mobile phone with a messaging app.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which type of service provider would supply the internet connection?

options.content: A courier company
A wholesaler
An internet service provider
The regulator
options.rationale: The regulator licenses providers; it does not sell connections.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** advantages to Nyasha's shop of using email and a messaging app.

points.description: Written record of orders from contractors.
Fewer mistakes and disputes than orders written down during calls.
Customers can contact the shop even when the landline is busy / send pictures of parts they need.
So fewer lost sales and faster service.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **one** problem Nyasha may face with the new services.

points.description: Problem identified, e.g. costs of data / power cuts / network problems / scams.
Explained.
Applied to the shop, e.g. orders not received during a power cut, losing customers.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Nyasha should keep the landline once the new services are installed. Justify your answer.

points.description: Reason to keep: published number customers know / works when mobile network weak.
Reason to drop: saves line rental; mobile phone and apps do the same job.
Considers back-up during network or power problems.
Justified recommendation.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Many customers already know the landline number, and it gives a back-up if the mobile network is weak. On the other hand, the mobile phone and messaging app can take calls and orders, so the landline's rental may be wasted. Nyasha should keep the landline for at least a few months while customers learn the new contacts, then review how often it is used.

explanation: Email and messaging give records and more ways to reach the shop, but bring costs and depend on power and networks.
hints: (b) Think about records and the engaged line.
(d) Weigh cost against reliability and customers' habits.

stem: Sipho has a small farm near Chinhoyi and sells vegetables to restaurants in Harare. A friend says that "with a mobile phone and the internet, Sipho no longer needs to visit his customers at all".

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **two** telecommunication services Sipho could use to sell his vegetables.

points.description: One service, e.g. voice calls / SMS / messaging app / email.
A second service, e.g. social media page / mobile money / website.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** limitations of relying only on telecommunication to deal with his customers.

points.description: No personal contact: harder to build trust and relationships.
Customers may switch to suppliers they know personally.
Cannot show quality of fresh produce as well as in person / misunderstandings.
Network or power problems may stop orders arriving.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Discuss whether Sipho's friend is right.

points.description: Telecommunication saves travel time and cost; orders and payments can be handled remotely.
Quick response to orders; photographs of produce can be sent.
But relationships and trust need some personal contact, especially with new customers.
Quality complaints and price negotiations may be easier face to face.
Network and power problems are a risk.
Justified conclusion (e.g. mostly by phone, with occasional visits).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Telecommunication saves Sipho time and money: restaurants can order by message, he can send photographs of the day's produce and receive payment by mobile money. However, restaurant owners buy from suppliers they trust, and occasional visits help him build relationships, deal with complaints and win new customers. Network or power failures could also stop orders. The friend is partly right: Sipho can handle routine orders by phone, but he should still visit customers from time to time, especially new ones.

explanation: Telecommunication handles routine trade efficiently but does not fully replace personal contact.
hints: (b) What does a phone call or message lack compared with a visit?
(c) Separate routine orders from building relationships.
